title: Italian Chef Fired for Refusing to Make Pineapple Pizza
paragraphs: What are your favorite pizza toppings? Maybe extra cheese? How about pineapple?
Few pizza toppings have caused as much disagreement as pineapple. While some people love how the sweet fruit goes with the salty ham, others believe pineapple has no place on pizza.
One Italian chef working in Australia is clearly in the second group.
Davide Tamburella was fired from La Costa restaurant in Brisbane in May this year after several disagreements with his bosses. One was his refusal to make ham-and-pineapple pizzas for a large event.
Tamburella said adding the fruit to pizza was an "insult to his culture." According to Australia's Fair Work Commission, it was the third time in four years that he had refused to make such pizzas.

The event was expected to bring in more than $10,000. Restaurant owner Elliot Ingram said that although pineapple wasn't his favorite topping either, giving customers what they wanted was part of the job.
The restaurant had other complaints about Tamburella, however, including his language and behavior at work.
Tamburella later took his case to the commission, saying that he had been unfairly fired. However, the commission rejected it because he had filed it too late.
La Costa closed in July, but Tamburella has since found work at another Brisbane restaurant. And, perhaps unsurprisingly, pineapple pizza isn't on its menu.
